clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A charge nurse instructs an RN to use medication left in a single-dose vial that was already used for another client. The RN explains that the vial is labeled for single-patient use, but the charge nurse repeats the instruction. What should the RN do?

options.A: Do not reuse the vial; obtain a new single-dose vial and escalate through the chain of command if the unsafe direction persists.
options.B: Use the opened vial for the second client with a new sterile syringe and needle after disinfecting the access diaphragm again.
options.C: Transfer the leftover medication into a new sterile syringe for the second client, then discard the vial after preparing the dose.
options.D: Use the opened vial for the second client if the medication looks clear and a new sterile needle and syringe are used for withdrawal.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC safe-injection guidance states that medications intended for single use, including single-dose vials, must not be used for more than one patient. CDC specifically states that a single-dose vial is approved for one patient for one case, procedure or injection and that leftover contents should not be retained or used for another patient. A new sterile syringe and needle do not make reuse of a single-dose vial for a second patient acceptable. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan includes applying infection-prevention principles and, under Advocacy, acting as a client advocate and appropriately using resources such as the chain of command. Because the immediate charge nurse has repeated an unsafe instruction after the concern was raised, the RN should refuse to reuse the vial, obtain an appropriate new supply, and continue escalation through the organization's chain of command if the direction remains unresolved. Therefore A is the uniquely best answer.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Protect clients from unsafe injection practices by limiting single-dose vials to one patient and using the chain of command when an unsafe direction remains unresolved after initial advocacy.

scope_exclusions.multidose_vials: The stem explicitly identifies a single-dose vial. Rules for appropriately handled multidose vials are not tested or generalized.
scope_exclusions.compounding_exception: The item does not address pharmacy subdivision or sterile compounding under USP standards. It addresses bedside reuse of leftover contents from a single-dose vial already used for another client.
scope_exclusions.local_chain_structure: No specific supervisor title or escalation sequence is asserted; organizations may structure the chain of command differently.
scope_exclusions.disciplinary_action: The item does not prescribe disciplinary action against the charge nurse. It tests client protection and escalation of an unresolved unsafe instruction.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub search for 'single dose vial another patient chain command' returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank rescan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. It follows CDC single-dose-vial guidance and uses the NCSBN-supported chain of command when the immediate unsafe direction remains unresolved.
option_audit.B: Plausible because new sterile injection equipment is required for each patient, but new equipment does not permit reuse of a single-dose vial for a second patient.
option_audit.C: Plausible because a sterile syringe is appropriate for medication preparation, but transferring leftover medication does not convert a single-patient vial into medication suitable for another patient.
option_audit.D: Plausible because visual inspection and sterile equipment matter in medication preparation, but neither changes the single-patient restriction of a single-dose vial.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. The vial is explicitly single-dose and has already been used for another client, while the unsafe direction has already been challenged once. B, C and D all reuse the vial for a second patient; A alone protects the second client and addresses the unresolved unsafe instruction.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. All four alternatives are within seven characters and use parallel medication-preparation or safety actions; the correct answer is not length-cued.
